questions.q: A light ray is incident, at an incident angle ${\theta}_{1}$, on the system of two plane mirrors ${M}_{1}$ and ${M}_{2}$ having an inclination angle $75 °$ between them (as shown in figure). After reflecting from mirror ${M}_{1}$ it gets reflected back by the mirror ${M}_{2}$ with an angle of reflection $30 °$. The total deviation of the ray will be _____ degree.
questions.solution:
From the above figure, ${i}_{2} = 30 °$,

Now,

$∠ OBA + ∠ ABR + ∠ RBP = 180 ° ⇒ 2 ∠ OBA + 60 ° = 180 ° ⇒ ∠ OBA = 60 °$

In triangle $OAB$,

$∠ OBA + ∠ AOB + ∠ OAB = 180 ° ⇒ 60 ° + 75 ° + ∠ OAB = 180 ° ⇒ ∠ OAB = 45 °$

And,

$∠ OAB + ∠ BAI + ∠ IAQ = 180 ° ⇒ 2 ∠ OAB + 2{i}_{1} = 180 ° ⇒ {i}_{1} = 45 °$

Now the total deviation of the ray will be,

$\delta = 360 ° - 2\left({i}_{1} + {i}_{2}\right) ⇒ \delta = 360 ° - 2\left(30 ° + 45 °\right)\delta = 210 °$

$\delta = 360 ° - 2\left({i}_{1} + {i}_{2}\right) ⇒ \delta = 360 ° - 2\left(30 ° + 45 °\right)\delta = 210 °$

questions.q: An unpolarized light beam is incident on the polarizer of a polarization experiment and the intensity of light beam emerging from the analyzer is measured as $100$ Lumens. Now, if the analyzer is rotated around the horizontal axis (direction of light) by $30 °$ in clockwise direction, the intensity of emerging light will be _______Lumens.
questions.solution:
Assuming initially axis of Polarizer and Analyzer are parallel

Now emerging intensity $= \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}\cos^{2}30 °$

$= 100{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}^{2} = 100 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 75$

questions.q:
In the given figure, the face $AC$ of the equilateral prism is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $n$. For incident angle $60 °$ at the side $AC$, the refracted light beam just grazes along face $AC$. The refractive index of the liquid $n = \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{4}$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
(Given refractive index of glass $= 1 . 5$)
questions.solution:
When the refracted light just grazes the boundary the incident angle is called a critical angle.

Using snell's law at face $AC$.

$1 . 5sin60 ° = n \times sin90 °$

$⇒ 1 . 5 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = n = \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{4}$

$⇒ 3\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{x}$

$⇒ x = 27$

questions.q: Sodium light of wavelengths $650nm$ and $655nm$ is used to study diffraction at a single slit of aperture $0 . 5mm$. The distance between the slit and the screen is $2 . 0m$. The separation between the positions of the first maxima of diffraction pattern obtained in the two cases is _____ $\times {10}^{- 5}m$
questions.solution:
The condition for maxima in diffraction is,

$bsin\theta = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$.

For the first maxima $n = 1$. Therefore,

$bsin\theta = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2} ⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2b} = \dfrac{y}{D}y = \dfrac{3\lambdaD}{2b}$

Now the difference between the positions of the maxima will be,

${y}_{1} - {y}_{2} = \dfrac{3D}{2b}\left({\lambda}_{1} - {\lambda}_{2}\right) ⇒ {y}_{1} - {y}_{2} = \dfrac{3 \times 2}{2 \times 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} \times \left(655 - 650\right) \times {10}^{- 9} = 3 \times {10}^{- 5}m$

questions.q: A beam of light consisting of two wavelengths $7000\overset{o}{A}$ and $5500\overset{o}{A}$ is used to obtain interference pattern in Young's double slit experiment. The distance between the slits is $2 . 5mm$ and the distance between the plane of slits and the screen is $150cm$. The least distance from the central fringe, where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide, is $n \times {10}^{– 5}m$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The given data is

${\lambda}_{1} = 7000\overset{o}{A}$

${\lambda}_{2} = 5500\overset{o}{A}$

$d = 2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

$D = 1 . 5m$

The path difference is given by

$n{\lambda}_{1} = m{\lambda}_{2}$

$7n = 5 . 5m$

$⇒ 14n = 11m ⇒ n = 11$ and $m = 14$

The formula for the distance of a bright fringe is

$y = \dfrac{n{\lambda}_{1}D}{d}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{11 \times 7 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 1 . 5}{2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$= 46 . 2 \times {10}^{- 4} = 462 \times {10}^{- 5}$

It is given that

$n \times {10}^{- 5} = 462 \times {10}^{- 5} ⇒ n = 462$

questions.q:
An object is placed at a distance of $12cm$ from a convex lens. A convex mirror of focal length $15cm$ is placed on another side of the lens at $8cm$ as shown in the figure. The image of the object coincides with the object.

When the convex mirror is removed, a real and inverted image is formed at a position. The distance of the image from the object will be $___cm$
questions.solution: For the object to coincide with the image, the light must fall perpendicularly to the mirror. This means that the light will have to converge at $C$ of the mirror. Without the mirror also, the light would coverage at $C$. So the distance is:$= 12 + 8 + 30 = 50cm$.
